templates_considered: AUTH-002 admin_endpoints_check_role: fit; the 'admin endpoints call role check first' ask. Used as the base, but its tags:[admin] scope matched nothing, because the admin api_group carries no tags. Switched to api_groups.

AUTH-020 own_records_only: partial fit at best. Its where-constraint rule pins compare_to to $auth.id, which the ask does not want (org isolation, not owner isolation). Title 'own records' would be misleading. Not used.
AUTH-010 endpoints_need_login: did not fit; the ask does not require login, it requires a role.
AUTH-030 no_self_promotion: did not fit; not about role writes.
CONF-010 sensitive_tables_need_login: did not fit; no table_tags for tenants and it is about login, not org filtering.
RET-001 audit_log_protected and CHG-001 endpoints_have_tests: not in the ask.

rules.covers: Admin endpoints check the role first, before doing anything else (placement first, not just any position).
Never touches tenants without filtering by org_id. No compare_to, because the ask gives no value and admins are cross-org.

ask_parts_not_covered.part: 'every endpoint under /admin': api/app/admin/stats_GET.xs is at /api:app/admin/stats, in the app group, and api_groups cannot select it by path. Not scoped in.
Whether the role check's result is 'admin' or 'support_lead' (what the check decides)
Org isolation for admins: should a support lead only reach tenants in their own org?
Tenant writes hidden inside called functions

assumptions: '/admin' means the admin api_group (served at /api:admin), not any path containing admin.
The role check is check_admin_role (function) and it already tests admin or support_lead.
'Filtering by org_id' means a predicate on the statement's own tenants table, with any value (no compare_to).
tenants.org_id is the field that holds the org (it is an int field linked to orgs).
confusions: AUTH-002 template fill says tags:[admin], but the workspace's admin api_group has no tags. The template's scope doesn't say whether api_groups is an allowed alternative for that check. I used it, and parse accepted it with no rule warning, but the guidance should say so.

The 'before anything else' wording maps to placement first. Ambiguous whether a precondition or a db.get before the check is a violation of 'first'. The check doc says first means the object's own first statement, a comment skipped, so it's clear, but the template summary says 'as its first statement' only.

Template AUTH-002 is keyed on the admin tag, so an endpoint that is under /admin but not tagged admin is silently not examined. The catalogue limits note says this, but a path-based scope would be a much better fit for 'every endpoint under /admin'. There is no path scope param.

The where_constraint check says db.edit passes only when picked by field against compare_to. A PATCH by id with no compare_to is therefore always a finding. That's correct for this ask but the reason is not obvious from the template for AUTH-020.
No template covers 'tenant isolation by org' directly. AUTH-020 is about owner/user, and its rule titles would mislead, so I wrote a custom key TEN-010 instead of a template key.
wished_for: A path or endpoint-name scope param (for example path_prefix: '/admin'), since the customer's words are about URLs.
A template or recipe for tenant/org isolation (multi-tenant row scoping) with an example that leaves compare_to empty for cross-org staff and sets it for normal users.
A note on whether api_groups counts as a substitute for tags in templates whose fill is tags.
A check that can see what a role check decides (or an example of pairing object.statement_required with a role-value check).
why_confidence: Both policies parse with no rule warnings, and the check semantics fit the ask for 'first' and 'org_id on tenants'. The gap is scope: 'under /admin' is matched by api_group, which may miss endpoints a customer thinks of as admin (app/admin/stats). And the role check verifies that the function is called first, not what it decides. Nothing was evaluated against the live workspace.
